item.title: PART 1: The Man Who Jailed 46 People Over a Cell Phone Now Runs Niagara Falls
item.description: Shortly after 9:00 AM on March 11, 2005, Judge Robert Restaino took the bench in Niagara Falls City Court. Approximately 70 people filled the courtroom—46 defendants in a domestic violence diversion program, plus attorneys, court staff, and counselors. For 45 minutes, proceedings went normally. item.title: The $1.5 Billion Project the Niagara Falls Mayor Doesn’t Want Residents to Know About
item.description: By Frank Parlato Kevin O’Leary stood at the podium at Data Center World 2025 in Washington, D.C., and declared the obvious to anyone paying attention: “This is the new gold rush.” The “Shark Tank” star was announcing Wonder Valley, a $2 billion AI-powered data center planned for Alberta. But he was also describing a global phenomenon. Thirty-six states have enacted laws to attract data center developers, including tax exemptions for equipment and construction materials and job-creation credits.
